input.quote: the right to use, a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated, with a direct Internet connection of shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth, plus capacity to process continuously during burst periods. HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.
input.rationale: Section 1.4 is the only grant running in our favour (access to and the right to use HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools). It names only "the Company", so our affiliates and the contractors who would operate and monitor the Site on our behalf are outside the grant, and nothing prevents HDI from revoking or suspending the access at will or on a change of control. That falls short of the playbook position that the licence extend to affiliates and contractors and not be revocable at the vendor's discretion. The licence we grant HDI in the "Deerskin" Marks (§6.1) is already non-exclusive, non-transferable and limited to carrying out its obligations, so no change is needed there. Redline adds affiliate/contractor coverage plus non-revocability absent our uncured material breach and successor coverage; fallback is affiliate coverage on written notice and successor transfer only.

proposal.summary: Extend the §1.4 access/use grant to our affiliates and contractors, and make it non-revocable absent our uncured material breach, with successor coverage.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the right to use the hosting system and administration tools to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, since they support the Site on our behalf, and confirmed HDI cannot revoke or suspend that access at will (only for our uncured material breach) and that it passes to a successor to our business.

ops.text: The access and rights to use granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall not be revoked, suspended or limited by HDI during the term of this Agreement, except in the case of a material breach by the Company that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written notice, and shall extend to any successor to the Company's business by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets.
